summary: Milman Parry was a linguistics scholar who studied at UC Berkeley, the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet, and Oakland Technical High School. He held an academic post at Harvard University from circa 1929 to 1935.

Milo Cleveland Beach is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Harvard. He held posts at the Fogg Art Museum, Boston's Museum of Fine Arts, Williams College, and served as Director of the National Museum of Asian Art.

Miloslav Krása was an Indology and history scholar who studied under Vincenc Pořízka at Charles University (1943–1947) and at the University of Allahabad. He served as a teacher at Charles University from 1954 to 1997.

Miloš Borecký worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Jan Rypka, later working as a librarian at the Czech National Library and at the Library of Congress.

Milton Singer was a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned his B.A. from UT Austin and his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago under Rudolf Carnap, where he later served as Professor of Anthropology from 1954 to 1979.

Min Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who was a postgraduate student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006). Lin is attested as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin pursued studies under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Min Thu Wun was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied under Pe Maung Tin at the University of Rangoon (~1926–1935) and pursued further studies at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Minakshi Banerjee is an Indology scholar who conducted doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar. As of 2026, she holds a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society.

Ming Chen is a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Chen held a professorship at Peking University, attested in 2001 and 2013, and taught Alexander O. Hsu, Weilin Wu, and Jinchao Zhao.

Ming Mei is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan. Mei also studied at SOAS under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and completed a Ph.D. at UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en, later serving as Professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Mingqian Xu is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an MA at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and a PhD at National Chengchi University. Xu was a Project Research Assistant at Dharma Drum from 2013 to 2015.
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Mini Verma is an Indology scholar who held lecturer and assistant professor posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, Sai Group of Institutions, Institute of Management Studies Noida, and Jagannath Institute of Management Sciences Noida.

Minori Nishimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami. Nishimura held academic posts at Taisho University, Sanko Cultural Institute, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Minoru Hara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo and president of ICPBS.
Minoru Inaba is a history and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. Inaba held posts at Tokuyama Corporation, Kyoto University, and Doshisha University.

Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1966 to 1999.

Minton Warren was a linguistics scholar who studied at Tufts, Yale, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg. He served as Associate Professor of Latin at Johns Hopkins, director of the American School of Classical Studies in Rome, and professor at Harvard.
